## Method A: Launcher Hub {#method-a-launcher-hub}

### Install for your operating system

Select your operating system to download the launcher and follow the step-by-step instructions:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Windows {#windows}

```{=html}
<div class="download-panel">
  <div class="download-row">
    <div class="download-row-info">
      <div class="download-row-title">Windows 10 / 11</div>
      <div class="download-row-meta">64-bit (x86_64) • ~28 MB installer</div>
      <p class="download-row-desc">Installer with a setup wizard — Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts are created for you. Portable, no-installer versions are also available on the releases page.</p>
    </div>
    <a href="https://github.com/lrncrd/PyPottery/releases/latest" class="btn-editorial-primary" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><i class="bi bi-download"></i> Download Windows Installer</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="install-steps-list">
  <div class="install-step-card">
    <div class="install-step-num">01</div>
    <div class="install-step-body">
      <div class="install-step-title">Download and run the installer</div>
      <p class="install-step-desc">
        Download <code>PyPottery-Launcher-Setup.exe</code> from GitHub Releases and run it. It's a normal
        installer with a setup wizard (Welcome → choose folder → Install → Finish) — no admin rights needed, it
        installs to your own user profile, and it registers a proper uninstaller in <strong>Add or remove
        programs</strong>.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="install-step-card">
    <div class="install-step-num">02</div>
    <div class="install-step-body">
      <div class="install-step-title">Launch it</div>
      <p class="install-step-desc">
        The installer already created a Start Menu entry and a Desktop shortcut for you. Open either one — it
        starts a local web server and opens your browser to <code>http://127.0.0.1:5000</code>.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="install-step-card">
    <div class="install-step-num">03</div>
    <div class="install-step-body">
      <div class="install-step-title">First-run environment setup</div>
      <p class="install-step-desc">
        Click <strong>"Configure Environment"</strong> in the browser interface. The launcher detects your GPU or
        CPU, provisions an isolated Python runtime, and installs the matching PyTorch build. Later launches start
        immediately.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-note}
#### Windows SmartScreen warning
GitHub release binaries aren't signed with an enterprise code-signing certificate, so Windows Defender
SmartScreen may show *"Windows protected your PC"*. Click **"More info"**, then **"Run anyway"**.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Prefer a portable version?
Two no-installer alternatives sit on the same [releases page](https://github.com/lrncrd/PyPottery/releases/latest):
`PyPottery-Launcher-Windows-v1.1.0.zip` (extract, then run `PyPottery.bat`) and
`PyPottery-Launcher-Windows-EXE-v1.1.0.zip` (extract, then run `PyPottery.exe` directly). Both skip the installer
entirely — useful on a locked-down machine. Unlike the installer, they don't create shortcuts for you; right-click
the executable and choose **Send to → Desktop (create shortcut)** if you want one.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="install-steps-list">
  <div class="install-step-card">
    <div class="install-step-num">01</div>
    <div class="install-step-body">
      <div class="install-step-title">Download the .dmg</div>
      <p class="install-step-desc">
        Download <code>PyPottery-Launcher-macos-arm64.dmg</code> (Apple Silicon: M1–M4) or

  <div class="install-step-card">

      <div class="install-step-title">Drag to Applications</div>
      <p class="install-step-desc">
        The .dmg opens a window with <code>PyPottery Launcher.app</code> next to an <code>Applications</code>
        shortcut — drag one onto the other. This is the standard macOS install, and it's what avoids Gatekeeper's
        "App Translocation" issue in the first place.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="install-step-card">
    <div class="install-step-num">03</div>
    <div class="install-step-body">
      <div class="install-step-title">Launch from Applications</div>
      <p class="install-step-desc">
        Open <code>PyPottery Launcher.app</code> from <code>/Applications</code>. On Apple Silicon, PyPottery
        initializes the Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) backend automatically. Environments, model caches, and
        logs live in <code>~/Library/Application Support/PyPottery</code>.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-note}
#### "Developer cannot be verified"
macOS may block software downloaded outside the App Store with *"PyPottery Launcher cannot be opened because the
developer cannot be verified"*.

- **GUI**: right-click (or Control-click) `PyPottery Launcher.app`, choose **Open**, then confirm.
- **Terminal**: clear the quarantine attribute:
  ```bash
  xattr -cr /Applications/"PyPottery Launcher.app"
  ```
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Opened it straight from Downloads?
If the app runs from a translocated or quarantined location instead of `/Applications`, PyPottery notices and
offers a dialog to move itself there for you — no manual Terminal work required. Installing from the `.dmg`
above avoids the situation from the start, since it's already pointing you at `/Applications`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Portable version
A plain `.zip` of the same app (<code>PyPottery-Launcher-macos-arm64.zip</code> /
<code>-x86_64.zip</code>) is also on the releases page, for anyone who'd rather place the app manually than use
the `.dmg`.
:::

```{=html}
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-note}
#### FUSE requirement on recent distributions
AppImage requires FUSE 2. Recent distributions (Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 40+) don't ship
`libfuse2` by default. If the AppImage fails to start:
```bash
# Ubuntu / Debian / Linux Mint:
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y libfuse2

# Fedora / RHEL:
sudo dnf install -y fuse-libs

# Arch Linux:
sudo pacman -S fuse2
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Prefer a plain directory to an AppImage?
`PyPottery-Launcher-linux-x86_64.zip`, on the same releases page, extracts to a normal directory instead — useful
if AppImages aren't an option on your system:
```bash
unzip PyPottery-Launcher-linux-x86_64.zip -d ~/PyPottery
cd ~/PyPottery
chmod +x PyPottery.sh install_desktop.sh
./install_desktop.sh   # optional: adds a menu entry
./PyPottery.sh          # installs missing dependencies on first run, then starts the launcher
```
:::

### First run and offline use

::: {.callout-important}
#### Offline use in the field
PyPottery runs **offline by default** once set up. The **first run** is the main exception: initial environment
setup and AI model downloads require an
internet connection.

One module-level exception applies beyond first run: PyPotteryLens currently uses a cloud LLM (OpenRouter) for
metadata extraction, so that specific feature needs a live connection every time it's used, not just once.
Everything else in the suite runs locally.
:::

### The Suite Launcher

The launcher is a local process supervisor reachable in the browser at `http://127.0.0.1:5000`.

```{=html}
<div class="simulator-wrapper">
  <div class="simulator-header-bar">
    <div class="simulator-title">
      <span class="simulator-indicator-dot"></span>
      <span>Launcher control panel walkthrough</span>
    </div>
    <span class="simulator-tag">Interactive</span>
  </div>
  <iframe src="animations/launcher_demo.html" class="launcher-simulator-iframe" title="PyPottery Launcher Interactive Demonstration"></iframe>
</div>
```

#### What it handles

1. **Environment lifecycle**: creates and validates an isolated virtual environment (`pypottery_env`), keeping tool dependencies separate from your system's global libraries.
2. **Hardware detection**: identifies available compute (CUDA 11.8–12.6, Apple Silicon MPS, AMD ROCm 6.2, or CPU) and installs the matching PyTorch build automatically.
3. **Single-instance lock**: an advisory lock  prevents duplicate processes or port conflicts; relaunching focuses the existing session instead.
4. **Offline model caching**: model weights are downloaded once into `models/` and cached for fully offline use afterward.
5. **Process isolation**: each application runs as an independent subprocess on its own loopback port. Closing the launcher stops all child processes.

## Method B: Source & CLI {#method-b-source-cli}
For running from a Git checkout or developing custom ML backends:

### 1. Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lrncrd/PyPottery.git
cd PyPottery
```

### 2. Create a virtual environment

```bash
python -m venv venv

# Windows:
venv\Scripts\activate

# macOS / Linux:
source venv/bin/activate
```

### 3. Install dependencies

```bash
pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 4. Enable Developer Mode

Developer Mode runs the launcher against your local Git checkout instead of downloaded release binaries:

1. Copy the template configuration:
   ```bash
   # Windows:
   copy launcher\dev_config.example.py launcher\dev_config.py

   # macOS / Linux:
   cp launcher/dev_config.example.py launcher/dev_config.py
   ```
2. In `launcher/dev_config.py`, set:
   ```python
   DEVELOPER_MODE = True
   ```
3. Run the development server:
   ```bash
   python -m launcher.gui
   ```

### 5. Standalone module installation

To run a single tool outside the launcher, see its dedicated installation guide:

- [PyPotteryLens](pypotterylens/index.qmd)
- [PyPotteryScan](pypotteryscan/index.qmd)
- [PyPotteryInk](pypotteryink/index.qmd)
- [PyPotteryTrace](pypotterytrace/index.qmd)
- [PyPotteryLayout](pypotterylayout/index.qmd)

## Troubleshooting

```{=html}
<div class="diagnostic-table-wrapper">
<table class="diagnostic-table">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="width: 25%;">Symptom</th>
      <th style="width: 35%;">Cause</th>
      <th style="width: 40%;">Resolution</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>"Windows protected your PC" (SmartScreen)</strong></td>
      <td>No enterprise code-signing certificate — common for open-source releases.</td>
      <td>Click <strong>"More info"</strong>, then <strong>"Run anyway"</strong>. One-time per release.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>"Developer cannot be verified" (macOS)</strong></td>
      <td>Gatekeeper flags apps downloaded outside the App Store or that aren't notarized.</td>
      <td>Right-click <code>PyPottery Launcher.app</code>, choose <strong>Open</strong>, confirm. Or run <code>xattr -cr /Applications/"PyPottery Launcher.app"</code>.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>"Move to Applications?" dialog (macOS)</strong></td>
      <td>Launched from a translocated/quarantined copy (e.g. still in <code>Downloads/</code>) instead of the installed copy in <code>/Applications</code>.</td>
      <td>Choose <strong>"Move to Applications"</strong> in the dialog, or drag the app there yourself and relaunch. Installing via the <code>.dmg</code> avoids this from the start.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>"AppImage requires FUSE to run" (Linux)</strong></td>
      <td>Recent distros (Ubuntu 24.04+, Fedora 40+) don't include FUSE 2 by default.</td>
      <td>Install it: <code>sudo apt install libfuse2</code> or <code>sudo dnf install fuse-libs</code>.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Permission denied on Linux</strong></td>
      <td>The executable bit wasn't preserved on extraction.</td>
      <td>Run <code>chmod +x</code> on the <code>.AppImage</code> file, or on <code>PyPottery.sh</code> if you're using the zip package.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Environment setup fails or is corrupted</strong></td>
      <td>Network interruption during the PyTorch download or package installation.</td>
      <td>Delete <code>pypottery_env/</code> (or <code>~/Library/Application Support/PyPottery/pypottery_env</code> on macOS) and re-run <strong>"Configure Environment"</strong>.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Port already in use</strong></td>
      <td>A previous instance crashed without releasing ports 5000–5005, or another local service is using them.</td>
      <td>Terminate orphaned Python processes via Task Manager, Activity Monitor, or <code>pkill -f "launcher.gui"</code> on Linux.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Deploying to a site with no connectivity</strong></td>
      <td>No internet access on-site for the first-run model and package downloads.</td>
      <td>Run the launcher and let all five apps and models download while still connected. Once initialized, everything except Lens's metadata extraction runs fully offline.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
</div>
```
